paragraphs: At the club hour, Leo sat at the library table and did not draw his cartoon. Teacher Kim saw that his pen was still on the paper, and she went to his chair. "Leo, what is the matter?" she asked. "My tooth is sore," said Leo. "It started last night, and it is worse now." "Yesterday he ate three sweet cakes at the market," said Lily. "Only two," said Leo. "The third one was very small."

Teacher Kim took Leo to the nurse's room. Nurse Jill asked him to sit down and said, "Tell me about your tooth." "It is at the back on the left," said Leo. "Is the pain there all day?" asked Nurse Jill. "No, only when I drink something cold or eat something sweet," said Leo. "Do you feel hot or tired?" she asked. "No, I feel fine," said Leo. "I am fit, and I play football every week."

Nurse Jill looked at his tooth with a small light. "I can see a small dark place," she said. "Do you brush your teeth every morning and every night?" "Every morning," said Leo. "At night, I am sometimes too tired." "Sweet food and no brushing are not good for your health," said Nurse Jill. "The pain goes to your brain, and your brain tells you to be careful with this tooth." "My brain says ouch, but my mouth says more cake," said Leo. Nurse Jill laughed.

Then Leo put one hand on his chest. "My heart is going fast," he said. "I am afraid of the dentist." "Many people are afraid," said Nurse Jill in a kind voice. "Your tooth is not serious, but a dentist must look at it." "A dentist's job is to help your teeth." "Take a slow breath with me." They breathed slowly three times, and Leo's heart went slower.

Nurse Jill opened a white cabinet and took out a new toothbrush. "This is for you," she said. "Here is my advice: brush your teeth tonight, and brush them again in the morning." She wrote a note for Leo's mom about the dentist. Afterwards, in the library, Leo took his pen again. He drew a cartoon of a small tooth with a big toothbrush, and he wrote "Captain Brush" above it. Lily laughed at the drawing and said, "That is for the blog."

sentences.text: At the club hour, Leo sat at the library table and did not draw his cartoon.
Teacher Kim saw that his pen was still on the paper, and she went to his chair.
"Leo, what is the matter?" she asked.
"My tooth is sore," said Leo.
"It started last night, and it is worse now."
"Yesterday he ate three sweet cakes at the market," said Lily.
"Only two," said Leo.
"The third one was very small."
Teacher Kim took Leo to the nurse's room.
Nurse Jill asked him to sit down and said, "Tell me about your tooth."
"It is at the back on the left," said Leo.
"Is the pain there all day?" asked Nurse Jill.
"No, only when I drink something cold or eat something sweet," said Leo.
"Do you feel hot or tired?" she asked.
"No, I feel fine," said Leo.
"I am fit, and I play football every week."
Nurse Jill looked at his tooth with a small light.
"I can see a small dark place," she said.
"Do you brush your teeth every morning and every night?"
"Every morning," said Leo.
"At night, I am sometimes too tired."
"Sweet food and no brushing are not good for your health," said Nurse Jill.
"The pain goes to your brain, and your brain tells you to be careful with this tooth."
"My brain says ouch, but my mouth says more cake," said Leo.
Nurse Jill laughed.
Then Leo put one hand on his chest.
"My heart is going fast," he said.
"I am afraid of the dentist."
"Many people are afraid," said Nurse Jill in a kind voice.
"Your tooth is not serious, but a dentist must look at it."
"A dentist's job is to help your teeth."
"Take a slow breath with me."
They breathed slowly three times, and Leo's heart went slower.
Nurse Jill opened a white cabinet and took out a new toothbrush.
"This is for you," she said.
"Here is my advice: brush your teeth tonight, and brush them again in the morning."
She wrote a note for Leo's mom about the dentist.
Afterwards, in the library, Leo took his pen again.
He drew a cartoon of a small tooth with a big toothbrush, and he wrote "Captain Brush" above it.
Lily laughed at the drawing and said, "That is for the blog."
